title: Infra GPU Fleet Capacity, Cloud Accounts, IaC Modules and CI/CD Runbook
author: Maya Patel
content:
Summary:
This runbook consolidates the operational guidance, Terraform/IaC module references, CI/CD pipeline patterns, cloud account networking notes, and capacity-planning model for the GPU fleet. It is intended for Infra engineers, SREs, and platform owners responsible for provisioning, scaling, and operating Redwood’s inference capacity across cloud regions.

Goals:
- Provide a single, actionable reference for provisioning and scaling GPU capacity.
- Standardize Terraform/IaC modules and their expected inputs/outputs.
- Document CI/CD guardrails, tests, and rollout patterns for infra changes.
- Capture common runbook playbooks for incidents related to GPU capacity, quota exhaustion, and account/network failures.

1) Ownership and Contacts
- Primary owner: infra-gpu-team (pager: infra-gpu-oncall)
- Secondary owner: infra-networking
- Priority escalation: SRE lead -> Head of Infra -> Platform Eng manager
- Slack: #infra-gpu, #infra-ops, pager duty: infra-gpu-oncall

2) Overview of GPU Fleet Components
- Control plane: cluster control services (autoscaler, placement controller, health-checker).
- Compute: GPU node pools (instance families per cloud region).
- Orchestration: k8s (managed) + custom node-allocator service.
- Storage: model artifact store (S3-compatible), ephemeral local NVMe for model cache.
- Networking: VPC per environment with shared transit for cross-region replication.

3) GPU SKUs and Standardized Node Pools
Table: Standard node pool templates
| name | instance type | gpu | memory | recommended use | notes |
| gpu-small | g5.xlarge | 1xA10G | 32GB | dev / canary | low-cost, single model inference |
| gpu-standard | g5.4xlarge | 4xA10G | 128GB | general purpose | baseline for most hosted workloads |
| gpu-highmem | p4d.24xlarge | 8xA100 | 1.1TB | high-throughput, large models | reserved capacity (Dedicated) |

- Each pool has tags: env, region, team, cost-center.
- On-prem equivalents follow the same logical templates (labelled onprem:true).

4) Capacity Planning Model (SLA-driven)
Inputs required:
- 95th percentile QPS per route (from Redwood Console usage dashboards)
- Average tokens per request, tokens/sec per model profile (from profiling harness)
- Per-GPU throughput (tokens/sec) by model and quantization profile
- SLO headroom (default 20% spare capacity)
- Failure budget for regional failures (reserve 10% cross-region)

Sizing steps (high level):
1. For each model, compute required tokens/sec = QPS * avg_tokens * concurrency factor.
2. Convert tokens/sec to GPUs required = ceil(tokens/sec / tokens_per_gpu(model_profile)).
3. Add headroom (multiply by 1.2) and round to nearest node-pool unit.
4. Add cross-region reserve: ensure at least 90% of peak can be served if a single region fails (use cross-region autoscaling policies).

Example calculation (text):
- Route: text-gen-prod, QPS@95 = 75, avg_tokens=120, tokens_per_gpu=12k/sec => tokens/sec=9000 => GPUs=0.75 => schedule 1 GPU; apply 1.2 headroom => 1.2 -> round to 2 GPUs in gpu-standard pool.

5) Autoscaling and Placement Policies
- Policies are expressed in the placement controller CRD and reconciled by node-allocator. Typical fields:
  - min_replicas, target_utilization (tokens/sec per GPU), max_replicas, scale_step, cooldown_seconds.
- Recommended defaults for hosted routes: min=2, target_utilization=0.65, max=200, scale_step=10, cooldown=120s.
- Dedicated (reserved) pools: min=max=fixed commit size, autoscaler disabled.
- Burst capacity: configured as a separate transient pool (burst:true) with preemption policy allowing eviction of low-priority jobs.

6) Terraform / IaC Modules (repo structure and patterns)
- Repo layout (canonical):
  - modules/gpu-node-pool/ (creates node pool, IAM roles, autoscaler configs)
  - modules/networking/ (VPCs, subnets, route tables)
  - modules/cloud-accounts/ (org policy, billing exports, cross-account roles)
  - envs/<env>/<region>/main.tf (instantiates modules with env overrides)
  - pipelines/ (CI/CD pipeline definitions)

Module contract examples (table):
| module | inputs (required) | outputs (important) |
| modules/gpu-node-pool | name, region, instance_type, gpu_count_per_node, min_size, max_size, tags | node_pool_id, autoscaler_policy_id |
| modules/networking | vpc_cidr, region, public_subnets, private_subnets, nat_config | vpc_id, subnet_ids |

Best practices for modules:
- Keep modules idempotent and re-entrant.
- Validate inputs using terraform validate + tflint + checkov in CI.
- Use small, focused modules; avoid large monoliths.
- Export stable outputs for cross-module wiring; keep names consistent.

7) CI/CD and Build Patterns for Infra Changes
Pipeline stages (recommended):
1. Lint & Static Analysis: terraform fmt, terraform validate, tflint, checkov.
2. Unit-style checks: module unit tests (terratest or kitchen-terraform).
3. Plan: run terraform plan in ephemeral workspace, post plan to PR with diff summary.
4. Guardrails: auto-detect any quota/budget changes and block if exceeding thresholds (quota changes must be approved via Infra Change Board).
5. Integration: apply to staging using pipeline service account (requires PR merge + manual approval for production).
6. Post-apply checks: smoke-tests (create ephemeral cluster and run model-profile smoke), policy checks, and tagging verification.

CI specifics and example commands:
- terraform workspace new <env-region> || terraform workspace select <env-region>
- terraform init -backend-config=path/to/backend.hcl
- terraform plan -var-file=env.tfvars -out=plan.tfplan
- terraform apply "plan.tfplan"

Secrets and state management:
- Remote state stored in encrypted object storage with state locking (DynamoDB/CloudLock).
- Pipeline uses short-lived service principals (OIDC) with least privilege.
- KMS keys per environment; access controlled via IAM roles and granted to the pipeline role.

8) Cloud Accounts & Networking Notes
- Account model: per-environment accounts (dev, staging, prod) with dedicated prod accounts for each major region.
- Central org account hosts shared services (logging, billing, security hub).
- Cross-account roles: create read-only and deploy roles with scoped permissions; rotate trust principals quarterly.
- Networking: strict CIDR allocations, Transit Gateway for inter-region model replication, centralized NAT gateways to control egress.

Network checklist when onboarding new region/account:
1. Create org account and enable billing export.
2. Provision VPC using modules/networking with tagged resources.
3. Register account in inventory (account-id map).
4. Set up shared logging and security forwarding.
5. Configure cross-region replication and routes for model artifact bucket.

9) Runbooks (operational playbooks)
Playbook: GPU capacity exhaustion (95th percentile saturation)
1. Detect: alert triggers (SLO breach, sustained >85% utilization for 10m).
2. Triage: check autoscaler metrics, pending pods, quota errors, node health.
3. Immediate mitigation:
   a. Increase target_replicas for affected placement -> scale step + apply via pipeline quick-path.
   b. Switch traffic to secondary region using routing policy (Console route failover).
   c. If quota limit hit, trigger cloud support ticket and activate short-term burst pool with preemptible instances.
4. Root cause: review model-level traffic, recent deploys, and any infra changes in last 24h.
5. Follow-up: update capacity model, schedule reserved capacity purchase if sustained.

Playbook: Node pool/network incident (node group failing health checks)
1. Detect: node pool degraded, >10% nodes NotReady for 5m.
2. Triage: check cloud provider status, autoscaler events, node logs (dmesg, kubelet).
3. Mitigation steps:
   a. Roll new nodes by increasing desired and draining old nodes.
   b. If due to kernel/OOM or driver issue, revert recent AMI/kernel/driver rollouts and pin to last known good.
   c. Use pre-baked AMI with validated NVIDIA drivers for quick remediation.
4. Follow-up: run postmortem if incident TTI > 30m or customer impact observed.

10) Safety and Rollout Patterns
- Canary pattern: deploy to a dedicated canary pool (1-2 nodes) and run synthetic traffic for 30m; monitor error rates and P50/P95 latencies.
- Progressive rollout: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% with automated rollback on error thresholds (error_rate > 1% or latency regressions > 15% at p95).
- Emergency rollback: pipeline has a pinned terraform state snapshot and an automated apply path to revert to previous node-pool sizes and AMI.

11) Operational run cadence and runbook drills
- Weekly: infra-gpu oncall review (capacity changes, quota usage)
- Monthly: capacity forecast sync with product (traffic trends, upcoming model onboards)
- Quarterly: disaster recovery drill (region failover and cross-region traffic shift)
- Annually: reserved capacity contract review and cloud vendor discounts negotiation.

12) Diagnostics and Observability (what to check during incidents)
- Metrics: cluster_gpu_utilization, tokens_per_second, pod_pending_count, node_notready_count, autoscaler_events_rate.
- Logs: node exporter, kubelet, node-allocator, placement-controller.
- Traces: request latency traces per model; sample traces for cold start vs warm cache.
- Dashboards: per-region capacity, per-model latency/throughput, cost per token.

13) Common Terraform PR checklist (merge blocker runbook)
- Module changes must include updated module changelog and version bump.
- Plan output size and resource diff reviewed for unexpected replace/create cycles.
- Any change that increases quota/ spend > $Xk/month (finance threshold) requires finance review.
- Security checks: ensure no IAM wide-open policies, no hard-coded secrets.

Appendices
A. Example TF variables snippet (env.tfvars):
```
region = "us-west-2"
instance_type = "g5.4xlarge"
min_size = 2
max_size = 20
tags = { env = "prod", team = "infra-gpu" }
```

B. Quick commands for oncall (production escalation):
- Check autoscaler events: kubectl -n infra logs deploy/placement-controller | grep autoscaler
- View nodes and GPU allocation: kubectl get nodes -o wide --label-columns=gpu_count
- Trigger scale-up quick path: infractl scale node-pool --id <node_pool_id> --desired  <n>

C. Links and references:
- Infra IaC guide: /confluence/eng-infra/terraform-and-iac/infra-iac-and-gpu-fleet-guide-2026
- GPU runbook: /confluence/eng-infra/runbooks/gpu-capacity-and-infra-runbook-2026
- Module registry: internal-module-registry.redwood.local

Notes and next steps:
- Short-term: add automated benchmark job post-plan that estimates tokens/sec change per plan diff.
- Medium-term: integrate quota-aware planner into CI to surface quota increases before apply.
- Long-term: unify capacity model across hosted and dedicated offerings for consistent cost reporting.
